author: priya
title: Message broker for payment events: Kafka vs RabbitMQ
body:
From: Priya Nair <priya.nair@contoso-payments.com>
To: ravi.kumar@contoso-payments.com
Date: 2025-03-12 09:15 UTC
Subject: Message broker for payment events: Kafka vs RabbitMQ

Team, I have been comparing Kafka and RabbitMQ for the payment event bus (authorised, captured, settled). My recommendation is Kafka. Reasons: (1) event replay. Settlement reconciliation needs to re-process a day of events after a bank file fix, and Kafka's retained log gives us that for free, RabbitMQ deletes messages once acked. (2) Ordering per merchant. Keying by merchant id gives strict ordering per merchant on a partition, which RabbitMQ only gives with a single consumer. (3) Throughput headroom. Projected volume is about 10x in 18 months and Kafka scales by partitions.

---

From: Ravi Kumar <ravi.kumar@contoso-payments.com>
To: priya.nair@contoso-payments.com
Date: 2025-03-12 11:40 UTC
Subject: Message broker for payment events: Kafka vs RabbitMQ

Makes sense for the consumers I own. One concern: RabbitMQ is simpler to run. Who operates the Kafka cluster?

---

From: Priya Nair <priya.nair@contoso-payments.com>
To: ravi.kumar@contoso-payments.com
Date: 2025-03-12 13:05 UTC
Subject: Message broker for payment events: Kafka vs RabbitMQ

Fair. The platform team already runs a shared Kafka cluster, so we get managed ops and don't carry the pager for brokers. That was the deciding factor for me. We lose the simple per-message routing of RabbitMQ and accept more consumer-side code.

---

From: Priya Nair <priya.nair@contoso-payments.com>
To: ravi.kumar@contoso-payments.com
Date: 2025-03-13 08:50 UTC
Subject: Message broker for payment events: Kafka vs RabbitMQ

I also looked at Pulsar. Rejected: smaller ecosystem here and no platform-team support. Decision criteria were replay, per-merchant ordering, and who runs it. Kafka wins on all three.

---

From: Ravi Kumar <ravi.kumar@contoso-payments.com>
To: priya.nair@contoso-payments.com
Date: 2025-03-13 09:30 UTC
Subject: Message broker for payment events: Kafka vs RabbitMQ

Agreed. I'll start on the consumer side once the topics are provisioned.

author: arjun
title: Re: Kafka operational risk
body:
From: Arjun Mehta <arjun.mehta@contoso-payments.com>
To: priya.nair@contoso-payments.com
Date: 2025-03-18 10:00 UTC
Subject: Re: Kafka operational risk

Priya, support concern on Kafka. If the consumer lags or dies, settlement input is late and I get the call. How do we recover?

---

From: Priya Nair <priya.nair@contoso-payments.com>
To: arjun.mehta@contoso-payments.com
Date: 2025-03-18 12:20 UTC
Subject: Re: Kafka operational risk

Good question, and part of why replay mattered. If the consumer falls behind, we reset the consumer group offset to the last good checkpoint and replay. No data loss. We'll add a lag alert at 5 minutes. I accepted the extra operational complexity in exchange for exactly this recoverability.

---

From: Arjun Mehta <arjun.mehta@contoso-payments.com>
To: priya.nair@contoso-payments.com
Date: 2025-03-18 12:45 UTC
Subject: Re: Kafka operational risk

OK, that helps. Please make sure the lag alert goes to the support channel.
